- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to lower levels after initial high peaks, but not always in sync with true price behavior.
- Late-period forecasts (last 10 days) are often too low, indicating underestimation of downward trends or delayed correction.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — true price declines occur before model adjusts.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to overreaction to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 15–25 day range.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the first 5–7 days, then gradually correct — but often too late or too much.
- Model fails to capture the true “tail” of price corrections — often underestimates the depth of drops after peaks.
- Forecasts are not calibrated to the true volatility structure — overconfident in short-term trends, underestimating long-term mean reversion.
